deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (from the previous page, folio 40r). Riemann has a triple (α, α_1, α_2) and three involutive substitutions, each fixing two entries and replacing the third by a Vieta-type expression: α_1' = 2αα_2 − α_1, α_2' = 2αα_1' − α_2, and α'' = 2α_1α_2 − α. With α fixed, the sequence u_0 = α_1, u_1 = α_2, u_2 = α_1', u_3 = α_2', u_4 = α_1'', … obeys the Chebyshev recurrence u_{n+1} = 2α u_n − u_{n−1}. He had found the continued fraction α_1/α_2 = 2α − 1/(2α − …) with fixed point z = α ± sqrt(α²−1). The same page carries a second-order ODE ∂²y/∂e² = ψ(λ) y with a parameter κ and Wronskian-type quantities. This suggests, but does not prove, that the α's are half-traces of monodromy or transfer matrices. The next page differentiates with respect to a parameter x.

THIS PAGE.

(a) Uniformising parameter. He sets 2α = ε + 1/ε, so the roots of z² − 2αz + 1 = 0 are ε^{±1}. The general solution is u_n = A ε^n + B ε^{−n}. From u_0 = α_1 and u_1 = α_2 [solved by me]: A(ε−1/ε) = α_2 − α_1/ε and B(ε−1/ε) = εα_1 − α_2. Several struck-out attempts at the top lead to the formula he keeps:
(ε−1/ε)·α_1' = (ε²α_2 − εα_1) − (ε^{−2}α_2 − ε^{−1}α_1).
This is equivalent to α_1' = (ε+1/ε)α_2 − α_1.

(b) The sign ‡. It is read here as 'goes over into under the substitution (α_1, α_2) → (α_1', α_2')', which is a shift by two steps (my interpretation). He writes:
• α_1(ε−1/ε) ‡ α_2(ε²−ε^{−2}) − α_1(ε−ε^{−1}), i.e. u_0 → u_2.
• α_2(ε−1/ε) ‡ α_2(ε³−ε^{−3}) − α_1(ε²−ε^{−2}), i.e. u_1 → u_3.
He then splits α_2(ε−1/ε) = (α_2ε − α_1) − (α_2ε^{−1} − α_1) and notes:
• Under the double shift the two pieces are multiplied by ε² and ε^{−2}.
• Under a single shift they are multiplied by ε and ε^{−1}.
In the left column he states this as the eigenvector property: α_2 − α_1/ε ‡ ε²α_2 − εα_1, and α_2 − εα_1 ‡ ε^{−2}α_2 − ε^{−1}α_1.

(c) Symmetric eigen-coordinates. He defines t = ε^{1/2}α_2 − ε^{−1/2}α_1 and t' = ε^{−1/2}α_2 − ε^{1/2}α_1. Then:
• α_2(ε−1/ε) = tε^{1/2} − t'ε^{−1/2}.
• α_1(ε−1/ε) = tε^{−1/2} − t'ε^{1/2}.
• Under the substitution, t → ε²t and t' → ε^{−2}t'.

(d) The invariant. He writes α_2² + α_1² − 2αα_1α_2 + α², the symmetric cubic later known as the Fricke/Markov-type form. He computes α_1α_2(ε−1/ε)² = t² + t'² − tt'(ε+1/ε). He then records tt' + ¼(ε+1/ε)², which [verified by me] equals α² + α_1² + α_2² − 2αα_1α_2, since tt' = α_1² + α_2² − 2αα_1α_2. Because tt' is invariant under t → ε²t, t' → ε^{−2}t', this exhibits the cubic as an invariant of the substitution.
He also expresses the third move 2α'' = 4α_1α_2 − 2α in t, t':
(4α_1α_2 − 2α)(ε−1/ε)² = −(ε+1/ε)(ε−1/ε)² + 4t² + 4t'² − 4(ε+1/ε)tt'.

(e) Left middle. He writes (ε_2 + 1/ε_2) − 1/(εε_1) − ε_1/ε (denominators as I reconstruct them), and the cleared form ε_2²εε_1 + εε_1 − ε_2 − ε_1²ε_2. The second is the first multiplied by εε_1ε_2. It equals (2α_2 − 2α_1/ε)·εε_1ε_2 if 2α_1 = ε_1 + 1/ε_1 and 2α_2 = ε_2 + 1/ε_2. This looks like an attempt to give all three α's their own ε-parameter (tentative).

(f) Dependence on a parameter x. Restating α_1' = 2αα_2 − α_1, α_2' = 2αα_1' − α_2 and α_1'' = 2αα_2' − α_1', he differentiates by the product rule:
• ∂α_2'/∂x = 2α∂α_1'/∂x − ∂α_2/∂x + 2α_1'∂α/∂x.
• ∂α_1''/∂x = 2α∂α_2'/∂x − ∂α_1'/∂x + 2α_2'∂α/∂x.
This prepares the next page, where 2∂α/∂x = (ε−1/ε)∂logε/∂x and log t is differentiated.

(g) Bottom. He expands the plain sum of squares α² + α_1'² + α_2'², not the full cubic. Using α_2'² = 4α²α_1'² − 4αα_1'α_2 + α_2² and 2αα_2 = α_1 + α_1', he obtains α_2² + α² + α_1'²(4α² − 1) − 2α_1'α_1. Riemann wrote the last term as −2α_1'α. The plain sum of squares is not invariant; this is exploratory.
errors: Bottom lines: substituting 2αα_2 = α_1 + α_1' into −4αα_2α_1' gives −2α_1'² − 2α_1α_1'. Riemann writes −2α_1'α (subscript on the second factor missing), and this slip is carried into the final line α_2² + α² + α_1'²(4α²−1) − 2α_1'α.

That bottom computation treats the plain sum of squares α² + α_1'² + α_2'², which is not invariant. The genuine invariant needs the term −2αα_1'α_2'. This is an exploratory dead end rather than a false claim.

Several struck-out lines at the top contain abandoned sign and factor attempts. All retained formulas (α_1' and α_2' in ε-form, the t, t' relations, the product formula, the 4α_1α_2 − 2α identity, and the derivative rules) check out.

results.what: Solution of the recurrence u_{n+1} = 2α u_n − u_{n−1} via 2α = ε + 1/ε, u_n = Aε^n + Bε^{−n}, with explicit diagonalisation of the substitution (α_1, α_2) → (α_1', α_2') (eigenvalues ε^{±2}, eigen-coordinates t, t').
results.modern_name: Chebyshev-type linear recurrence / diagonalisation of an SL(2) map; ε is the eigenvalue of a matrix with half-trace α

results.what: The cubic α² + α_1² + α_2² − 2αα_1α_2, shown to be invariant under the move α_1 → 2αα_2 − α_1 (written as tt' + α² with t → ε²t, t' → ε^{−2}t'). Combined with the other Vieta involutions on the previous page (α'' = 2α_1α_2 − α), this is the Markov/Fricke cubic with its Vieta-involution group.
results.modern_name: Fricke–Vogt trace invariant x² + y² + z² − xyz (in half-traces), i.e. the commutator trace; Markov-type cubic surface and Vieta involutions
results.usually_credited_to: Vogt (1889), Fricke (1896), Fricke–Klein; Markov (1879–80) for the Markov equation

results.what: Derivatives of the transformed quantities with respect to a parameter x (product rule), preparing an analysis of how the invariant and ε vary with a parameter.
results.modern_name: variation of trace coordinates along a deformation (cf. monodromy of a parametrised second-order ODE)

deep.surprise_reason: On this page alone the mathematics is elementary: diagonalising a Chebyshev recurrence and noting the conserved quadratic form. What makes it mildly notable is the context. Riemann writes the fully symmetric cubic α² + α_1² + α_2² − 2αα_1α_2 with the three Vieta involutions (previous page), next to second-order ODE and monodromy material. If the α's are half-traces of monodromy matrices, this anticipates the Fricke–Vogt trace identity and invariant (c. 1889–96). That interpretation is not proven on this page, so the rating stays conservative.

transcription_corrections: The symbol transcribed as '∓' throughout is not a sign. It is Riemann's mark (like ‡ or ⋕) meaning 'goes over into under the substitution'.
Left column: 'α_2 − α_1/ε ∓ ε²α_2 − εα_1 sd' should read 'α_2 − α_1/ε ‡ ε²α_2 − εα_1'. The next line is 'α_2 − εα_1 ‡ ε^{−2}α_2 − ε^{−1}α_1' (the struck item is εα_1).
Second ‡-line in the right column: 'α_2(ε − 1/ε) ‡ α_2(ε³−ε^{−3}) − α_1(ε²−ε^{−2})' (transcribed correctly). In the first line the first term is α_1(ε−1/ε).
Right column, lower ‡-line: the first term is (α_2ε − α_1), not (α_1ε − α_1). It reads (α_2ε−α_1) − (α_2ε^{−1}−α_1) ‡ (α_2ε−α_1)ε − (α_2ε^{−1}−α_1)ε^{−1}.
Left middle: for consistency with the following line ε_2²εε_1 + εε_1 − ε_2 − ε_1²ε_2, the expression must be (ε_2 + 1/ε_2) − 1/(εε_1) − ε_1/ε, without ε_2 in the denominators.
Bottom: '−2α_1'α' is as written by Riemann, but mathematically it should be −2α_1'α_1. The factor in the final line is (4α²−1).
